title.narrative: Cost savings to business due to Customs Reform

baseline.value: Inland Clearance (avg) 148 minutes. Border Clearance (avg) 46 minutes

target.value: Inland Clearance (avg) 105 minutes. Border Clearance (avg) 27 minutes

comment.narrative: <p>The average Customs only clearance times available from ASYCUDA data for three of the main ICDs (Jalalabad, Herat, and Hairatan), and at three main border crossings (Torkham, Islamqala and Torghundi) at the end of project were 67 minutes for inland clearance, and 20 minutes for border clearance. This far exceeds the revised end of project target of 105 minutes and 27 minutes for inland and border clearance respectively.</p>

title.narrative: Provision of selected Customs infrastructure to enable modernized operations

target.value: Improvement of (i) Jalalabad Inland Clearance Depot (ICD); (ii) Kabul ICD; (iii) Construction of Khost ICD; (iv) Nimroz ICD; (v) Torkham Border Post; (vi) Andkhoi ICD; (vii) Aqina Border Post. Contract awarded for an additional eight sub-projects at locations agreed between the World Bank and ACD in keeping with the overall results framework.

comment.narrative: <p>Target substantially met. 63 sub-project were completed in Kabul, Jalalabad, Khost, Farah, Abu Nasr Farahi, Kandahar, Kunduz, Andkhoi and Aquina.</p>

actual.value: Approximately 65 contracts of various sizes were awarded since the start of project. Major works included construction of an entirenew Customs ICD at Khost, Warehouses and truck parking at Jalalabad, Construction of boundary wall and truck parking at Abu Nasr Farahi, construction of ASYCUDA Data center, customer facilitation center at Kabul HQ, construction of truck parking and warehouses atNimroz, construction of truck parking and new administration building at Kandahar, and construction of overhead water tanks, water supply and electrical system at various custom location, and ASYCUDA offices at various locations. Two contracts i.e. construction of boundary wall at Aqina, and construction of 2nd Phase of truck parking at Nimroz could not be completed by project closing due to various reasons, having achieved approximately 90% physical progress. The remaining works was being taken up through Government’s own resources in the next budget cycle (2019). The project also completed a detailed feasibility on setting up of a Multimodal container freight station outside Jalalabad.

title.narrative: Technical assistance to support the development of an adequate regulatory, administrative and institutional framework for Customs

target.value: Technical assistance for the following areas provided (i) Legislative Review; (ii) Customs value added activities; (iii) Review of Customs Clearance Procedures; (iv) Customs Control; (v) Reorganization plan for ACD; (vi) Integration and Sustainability Strategy for the ASYCUDA Unit; (vii) Pay and pension reform package for ACD; (viii) Coordination and partnerships with other government agencies; (ix) International Customs Unit; (x) Monitoring GAAP activities, milestones and benchmarks supported by ICN; (xi) Post Clearance Audit Unit; and (xii) Tariff and Statistics Unit (TRSU). Contract awarded for (i) National Single Window feasibility, (ii) Trade Portal development (iii) Technology equipment feasibilities. Legislative review completed. Action Plan for setting up enforcement wing completed

comment.narrative: <p>While the component had contributed substantially, but a lot more could be done. This component in particular was effected by high turnover of International technical Advisor.</p>

actual.value: Considerable progress was achieved over the lifetime of the project, which included (i) Development of a long-term blueprint for Customs reforms in Afghanistan (ii) Development of ACD’s Five Year Strategic Plan for 2014-18; (iii) Development of a New Border Management Model; (iv) HR Policy for creation of Professional Customs Service; (v) Setting up International Customs Unit and Tax Research& Statistics Unit; (vi) technical assistance on implementing Risk Management (RM); (vii) Revision of Exemption Procedures; (viii) Strengthening of Valuation Unit for uniform valuation; (ix) strengthening Post Clearance Audit (PCA); (x) conducting User Perception Surveys; (xi) support to the Afghan National Customs Academy; (xii) Inter-Agency Collaboration; (xiii) award of contract for the feasibility study for implementing a National Single Window and Trade Information Portal; and (xiv) Proof reading of Pashto tariff bookand interpretation of explanatory notes.

title.narrative: Provision of selected Customs infrastructure to enable modernized operations

target.value: Contracts awarded for at least 8 sub-projects, and agreed Infrastructure works completed

actual.value: On infrastructure development, a total of 14 contracts of various sizes were awarded. Out of these 12 contracts have beencompleted. Only 2 contracts (Construction of Aqina Boundary Wall and Nimroz ICD Truck Parking) are still in progress, and will notbe completed by Project closing date. The main reason for the delay in completion of these two sub-projects were adverse weatherconditions, security related incidents, and delay in vacation of site by other security agencies, well beyond the control of ACD.

title.narrative: Technical assistance to support the development of an adequate regulatory, administrative and institutional framework for Customs

target.value:
Studies completed for (i) National Single Window feasibility, (ii) Trade Portal development (iii) Technology equipmentfeasibilities.
Experts hired for Legislative review, strengthening of PCA, valuation and risk management and enforcement.
ActionPlan for setting up enforcement wing completed

actual.value: The feasibility study for implementing a National Single Window and Trade Information Portal was awarded, and Consultants mobilizedin June. This activity will be transitioned, and undertaken through the on-going Fiscal Performance Improvement Support Project(FSP). Additionally the process to hire technical assistance in the areas of Risk Management, Enforcement, HR and Legal hascommenced. ACD has completed the drafting of regulations and procedures to implement the Cabinet approved HR policy.

title.narrative: Countrywide computerization of Customs Clearance operations

baseline.value: Declaration Processing System (DPS) operational at five locations (i) Kabul ICD, (ii) Kabul Airport, (iii) Herat, (iv) Mazar, (v) Kunduz

target.value: ASYCUDA DPS and wider modules Operational at 16 Custom offices. Risk Management operational at 11 locations. Valuation module operational at 6 locations.

comment.narrative:
<p>Achievements exceeded target.</p>

<p>End of Project target was ASYCUDA DPS Operational at 16 Custom offices. Achieved was 25 offices</p>

<p>End of Project target was Risk Management operational at 11 locations. Achieved was 19 offices</p>

<p>End of Project target was Valuation module operational at 6 locations. Achieved was 14 offices</p>

<p>Additional modules (Entry-Exit Gate, Cash Declaration, Vehicle Control, Electronic TIR etc.) also implemented at various offices.</p>

actual.value: ASYCUDA Declaration and wider modules were deployed at 25 Custom offices, including Kabul HQ, Kabul ICD, Kabul International Airport, Kabul Post, Nangrahar, Torkham, Balkh, Mazar Airport, Hairaatan, Sherkhan, Kunduz, Andkhoy, Herat, Herat Airport, Islamqala, Torghundi, Nimroz, Kandahar, Kandahar Airport, Paktia, Weesh, Nimroz, Abu Nasr Farahi, Farah and Khost. The end of project target was ASYCUDA deployment at 16 officies. Risk Management module has been deployed at 19 offices, while Valuation module at 11 offices.

title.narrative: Installation of executive information systems for Customs allowing real time monitoring of operations

baseline.value: Executive Information System not available in ACD

target.value: Executive Information System deployed at MOF, ACD HQ and five regional offices. Standard Alerts identified and generated. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for follow up action prepared and implemented.

comment.narrative: <p>Target mostly achieved. While the Executive Information System has been deployed at ACD HQ and four regional offices, and is also producing alerts and reports, however the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for follow-up action are yet to be finalized.</p>

actual.value: Executive information system was installed in ACD Headquarter, as well as four regional offices. Selected information via SMS was being provided to the ACD and MoF management. SMS Alerts were also being sent to traders confirming the amount of duty paid. The system was improved by including critical alerts. The system is also producing more than 26 types of reports.

title.narrative: Development of possible options for cross border Customs-to-Customs (C2C) Cooperation

baseline.value: No formal C2C cooperation between Afghanistan and its neighboring counties.

target.value: Real time data exchange between Afghan and Tajikistan Customs and Afghan and Pakistan Customs. C2C MoU between Afghanistan and Iransigned.

actual.value: Customs to Customs cooperation. Since last reporting period, the system interface between Iran Customs system and AfghanistanASYCUDA system was created and tested. Data exchange between Afghanistan and Pakistan is delayed due to various reasons, howeverboth sides have committed to complete the process at the earliest. The Bank Team is facilitating a mission to Pakistan within thenest couple of months to finalize the technical modalities. With MoU signed between with Iran, China and Uzbekistan, and real timedata exchange between Afghanistan and Tajikistan implemented, and data exchange between Afghanistan and Iran tested, the projecthas mostly met the end project target.

title.narrative: Development of possible options for cross border Customs-to-Customs (C2C) Cooperation

baseline.value: No formal C2C cooperation between Afghanistan and its neighboring counties.

target.value: C2C cooperation agreements signed between ACD and Iran, Pakistan and Tajikistan Customs. Real time data exchange started with Pakistan and Tajikistan Customs.

comment.narrative: <p>The project has exceeded the end of project target. ACD has been able to sign C2C agreements with eight countries, and real time data exchange functional between Afghanistan and Tajikistan Customs. The interface for real time data exchange between ACD and Iran Customs has also been developed, which was originally not a target. Real time data exchange with Pakistan couldn't commenc, mainly due to political reasons, but is expected to start by mid 2019. However Customs data exchange is taking place through the use of secure emails.</p>

actual.value: Customs to customs data exchange through secure emails were operational between Afghanistan and Pakistan from 2013. Since start of project, ACD has been able to sign Customs to Customs Cooperation agreements with Pakistan, Tajikistan, Iran, UAE, China, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan and Turkey. Real time data interface was developed between Afghanistan and Tajikistan, and data exchange formally commenced in May 2015. Interface has also been developed and tested between Afghan Customs ASYCUDA system and Iran Customs system. Realtime data exchange between Afghanistan and Pakistan yet to commence, however data exchange through secure email, and confirmation messages through Pakistan Customs WEBOC system is functional since 2013.

comment.narrative: <p>Three surveys were conducted by ACD, the first one in 2012, the second in 2015 and the last in 2017. The end of project target of 7 out of 10 user satisfaction score established in 2012 was met in the 2017 survey which gave a score of 7.4. All three surveys were conducted by independent consultant firms, covered four regions and over 400 users were interviewed.</p>

<p>The number of non-compliances detected through ASYCUDA Risk Management System (RMS), since its introduction in August 2013, started with a baseline of 5.5% with an end of project target of 7%. RMS is now functional at 19 Customs offices. However, the project was not able to achieve the target as at closing the number of detections reported through ASYCUDA RMS was only 3.1%. This is due to the selectivity criteria used to direct trucks to Red, Yellow or Green channel, was a commodity based criteria, was not dynamic, and was not being updated on a regular basis. This was resulting in a very high number of trucks being directed to Red channel for physcal inspection. Proper examination and inspection on such a high volume of trucks was not possible with the available resources, hence the number of detections remained low. However, very recently ACD has changed the selectivity criteria from commodity based to a more dynamic multi criteria risk assessment, and introduced this at four of the main Customs offices. The recent data has shown som improvements, with both reduction in trucks being directed to Red channel, and also by a slight increase in number of detections, leading to strong indication that the number of detections will increase significantly in the near future.</p>
